title: Iranian Officials Expect New U.S. Strikes or Tighter Sanctions as Trump Says He Will Hold Off for Now
dek: Trump has said he will hold off on fresh strikes, but an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator says Tehran expects military action or a harsher blockade.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electronic market-price display with rows of financial information

keyPoints: Trump said Tuesday he would hold off on fresh strikes on Iran for now, and the BBC reported he called more U.S. attacks "highly unlikely."

Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Telegram that Washington proposed a two-week timeframe before a decision on military action. The U.S. has not confirmed this.
Mohammadi said Iran rejected a request from Vice President JD Vance for a direct meeting with its negotiators.
Brent crude was at about $93 a barrel, according to the Guardian, while the U.S. has tightened its blockade of Iranian oil exports.
body:
Senior Iranian officials believe the United States is planning either further military strikes or a tighter economic squeeze, [the Guardian reported](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/11/trump-planning-military-assault-or-tighter-sanctions-iranian-officials). The assessment came from an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator, and it runs against public statements from the White House.

## Trump’s position

Trump said on Tuesday that he would hold off on fresh strikes for now, [CBC News reported](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-will-hold-off-on-fresh-iran-strikes-9.7416010). The BBC reported that he called further U.S. attacks "highly unlikely." Trump has also said the campaign had set Iran’s nuclear program back by decades, telling reporters it would take Tehran "25 years to rebuild," [the Jerusalem Post reported](https://www.jpost.com/american-politics/article-914616).

## Iran’s account

Mehdi Mohammadi wrote on his Telegram channel that the Americans had proposed a timeframe of about two weeks, after which Trump would decide on military action. He said Washington was preparing a limited strike and that Iran was already preparing a response. These are claims from one Iranian adviser; the Guardian described him as regarded as a reliable indicator of Ghalibaf’s thinking, but the U.S. has not confirmed the timeline.

Mohammadi also described the U.S. response to Iran’s proposals on reopening the Strait of Hormuz as unsatisfactory, and said Iran had rejected a request from Vance for a direct meeting before answering Tehran’s conditions for lifting the siege of the strait.

Iran also said it bombed a U.S. radar post on the Omani island of Didamar three days earlier. Meridian has not independently verified that claim.

## Economic pressure

The Guardian reported that the administration has settled on a strategy of economic pressure, tightening the blockade on Iranian oil exports while allowing other Gulf states’ shipments through Hormuz. Brent crude was about $93 a barrel, and Saudi oil production was near prewar levels of 9.3 million barrels a day.

Some Iranian officials fear that economic strain could spark renewed street protests, the Guardian reported, which could make a pre-emptive move more likely in Tehran.

Trump’s own remarks have varied in tone. Speaking on Tuesday, he said the war would end "soon" and that the world would be "a much safer and better place," according to a live report by Iran International.
